source_fields.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.

assumptions.description: The Bernoulli distribution family is known, but mu in (0,1)^K is hidden.
assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.

assumptions.description: A unique b satisfies mu_b>mu_i for every i different from b.
assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.

description_paragraphs: The fixed unknown mean vector satisfies $\mu\in(0,1)^K$ and has a unique best arm. Both means and individual arm gaps are hidden.
The data-dependent stopping time $\tau_\delta$ is measurable with respect to observed history and is not a fixed horizon.
The arm $\widehat{b}$ is recommended at stopping. Correctness must hold uniformly over all admissible mean vectors.

The comparison characteristic time $T^*(\mu)$ is defined by the allocation problem using forward $\operatorname{KL}(\nu_{\mu_i}\,\|\,\nu_{\lambda_i})$. It is an analytical benchmark, not an input supplied to the algorithm.

The full characteristic time $T^*(\mu)$ is defined by $T^*(\mu)^{-1}=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K}\inf_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}\sum_i w_i\operatorname{kl}(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$. The alternative class, Bernoulli KL divergence, and simplex are defined in the local notation table.
Require $K\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/2$. Both round actions and the final recommendation lie in $[K]$.
Take delta to zero with the instance mu fixed. Finite-parameter conclusions in which K or mu also vary are not part of this leading-constant comparison.
source_fields.instance: Arms have distributions $\nu_i=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_i)$, with $\mu\in(0,1)^K$ and unique best arm $b(\mu)$. The parameters $K$ and $\delta$ are public. The algorithm must be $\delta$-correct and stop almost surely on every admissible instance. Compare expected sample count at a fixed $\mu$.
interaction_timing: The environment fixes $\mu$. The values $K,\delta$ and the Bernoulli family are public.
Use the history to decide whether to continue; if continuing, select an arm before drawing one fresh sample.
The recommendation is returned at the history-dependent stopping time $\tau_\delta$.
Require error probability at most delta and almost-surely finite tau_delta for every admissible mu.
source_fields.parameter_domain_description: K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$, public; delta: $0<\delta<1/2$, public; mu: $\mu\in(0,1)^K$ with a unique largest coordinate, hidden or used only in analysis.
unresolved_applicability: Matching is verified for the leading constant as $\delta\to0$ with fixed $\mu,K$. It does not certify constants uniformly over all parameters at finite sample sizes.

source_fields.base_expression: The resource is E_mu[tau_delta]; the asymptotic comparison is E_mu[tau_delta]/log(1/delta), with mu and K fixed.
description_paragraphs:
$$
p_\mu(\mathcal{A}_\delta)=\Pr_\mu(\widehat{b}\ne b(\mu)),\qquad C_\mu(\mathcal{A}_\delta)=\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta].
$$

The identification loss is an error indicator, and expected stopping time is the cost. The asymptotic efficiency quantity $\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]/\log(1/\delta)$ is kept distinct from fixed-budget error probability.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The best-arm-identification model requires a unique best arm. Finiteness of expected stopping time and error-exponent endpoints follow the contract's specific conditions.
source_fields.normalization: Retain sample count, error probability, or relative asymptotic difficulty as defined here; do not rewrite them as cumulative regret.

auxiliary_interfaces: No additional oracle reveals means, gaps, optimal sampling proportions, or posteriors. Statistics, likelihood ratios, and allocation optimizations are computed internally from observed samples and the public model.
description_paragraphs: Bernoulli arm sampling:
Each call returns a fresh independent Bernoulli sample.
Arm choices depend only on the history; stopping and recommendation use information already obtained.
No extra samples are taken after stopping. This task has no regret-bearing action point.
Public inputs are K, δ, and the Bernoulli family. The means μ and gaps are hidden.

operations.access_schedule: Interaction follows the sequence in registry.protocols. Current loss feedback is available only after the action is submitted. Any pre-action disclosure of context or advice is specified separately.
operations.coupling: Each call returns a fresh independent Bernoulli sample. Arm selection depends only on the past, and stopping and recommendation use received information. No additional sampling occurs after stopping. This identification task has no regret-incurring action criterion.

feedback_quality.description: Each call returns a fresh independent Bernoulli sample. Arm selection depends only on the past, and stopping and recommendation use received information. No additional sampling occurs after stopping. This identification task has no regret-incurring action criterion.

operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and any probes permitted by the specification. The environment determines current losses, outcomes, or fresh samples. The learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order
operations.query_signature: Input: $a_t\in[K],\quad t\le\tau_\delta$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.

public_inputs: The Bernoulli distribution family is known; means and gaps are hidden.

source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: Output an almost surely finite stopping time $\tau_\delta$ and recommended arm $\widehat{b}\in[K]$. A computable correctness certificate is not required. No samples may be drawn after stopping.
source_fields.feasibility: Recommend one arm in $[K]$. Stopping and fixed-budget rules follow the declared protocol.

source_fields.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
source_fields.budget_semantics: The sample count $\tau_\delta$ is random, with primary cost $\mathbb E_\mu\tau_\delta$. There is no prespecified hard budget $T$.

components.description: The total sample count is the stopping time $\tau$; primary cost is $\mathbb E_\mu\tau$.
At most one generalized likelihood-ratio stopping test is performed after each fresh sample. This does not establish total arithmetic complexity.

description_paragraphs: Each arm pull yields one charged sample. The total number of samples is the random stopping time $\tau_\delta$, and the primary resource objective is the instancewise expectation $\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]$.
Any causal randomized algorithm that is uniformly delta-correct is allowed.

Track-and-Stop maintains empirical means, sample counts, and likelihood ratios and numerically computes allocation proportions. Those computations are not identified with one sample at no additional accounting cost.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.
source_fields.online_cost: Any causal randomized algorithm that is uniformly delta-correct is allowed. Track-and-Stop maintains empirical means, sample counts, and likelihood ratios and numerically computes allocation proportions. These computational operations are not identified with one sample at no additional accounting cost.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.
source_fields.scalarization: Retain the native objective and complete resource vector. At fixed $T$, compare cumulative regret. Best-arm-identification stopping times and error probabilities use their own task-specific criteria.
source_fields.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.

description_paragraphs: The algorithm adaptively samples Bernoulli arms, chooses a stopping time, and recommends the unique best arm. It must attain the prescribed confidence for every admissible mean vector. Cost is the expected number of samples on the instance; the central comparison concerns the leading constant as confidence tends to one for a fixed instance.
source_fields.goal_latex: \mathcal T_\delta(\mu)=\inf_{\mathcal A:\ \forall\lambda,\ \mathbb P_\lambda(\widehat b\ne b(\lambda))\le\delta,\ \mathbb P_\lambda(\tau_\delta<\infty)=1}\mathbb E_\mu[\tau_\delta],\qquad \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\frac{\mathcal T_\delta(\mu)}{\log(1/\delta)}

algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
description_paragraphs: Arbitrary causal randomized sampling, stopping, and recommendation rules are allowed. The algorithm must achieve the confidence guarantee uniformly over all admissible mean vectors and stop almost surely. Internal computation and storage are unrestricted.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable computation with exact real arithmetic is permitted; feedback complexity does not imply arithmetic or bit complexity. Any uniformly $\delta$-correct causal randomized algorithm is admissible. Track-and-Stop maintains means, sample counts, and likelihood ratios and numerically computes allocation proportions; these computations are not themselves sample observations.
algorithms.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.
algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
restrictions: Causal randomized algorithms must stop almost surely and have error probability at most delta for every admissible mu. Their inputs do not include mu, gaps, or the optimal allocation.

aggregation_order: First restrict to algorithms that are $\delta$-correct and stop almost surely for every admissible $\mu$.
Fix the target instance $\mu$ and arm count $K$, and compare $\mathbb E_\mu\tau_\delta$ over the stated algorithm class.
E_mu includes algorithmic randomness and every Bernoulli sample.
The verified comparison fixes mu and K and takes delta to zero in E_mu tau_delta/log(1/delta). It does not first take a worst case over mu.
guarantees.complete_expression: The native target is $\mathcal T_\delta(\mu)=\inf_{\mathcal A:\ \forall\lambda,\ \mathbb P_\lambda(\widehat b\ne b(\lambda))\le\delta,\ \mathbb P_\lambda(\tau_\delta<\infty)=1}\mathbb E_\mu[\tau_\delta],\qquad \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\frac{\mathcal T_\delta(\mu)}{\log(1/\delta)}$.
description_paragraphs: One algorithm family $\{\mathcal{A}_\delta\}$ must satisfy $\Pr_\mu(\widehat{b}=b(\mu))\ge1-\delta$ for every admissible mean vector $\mu$ and stop almost surely. Expected-cost guarantees are instancewise. In the limit $\delta\downarrow0$, hold $K$ and the entire $\mu$ fixed. Randomness includes sampling and the algorithm.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One δ-correct procedure for all μ, with μ and K held fixed when δ→0.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The variable $\tau_\delta$ is a measurable stopping time. The risk level $\delta$ is public; no fixed horizon $T$ is supplied. Correctness holds for every admissible instance.
